title: Quiz challenge: beat the clock (9:16)
description: A 21.6-second beat-the-clock quiz short: 2-4 shared answers sit at the bottom as labelled bins; five times a card drops in, a ring counts down 3-2-1 with ticks, the right bin lights up with a chime and confetti, the answer and a one-line reason appear, and the card falls into its bin. The outro recaps every answer, asks for the viewer's score (comment bait) and closes on a call to action and link. Code-rendered (scene.quiz-challenge) on a 112.5 bpm grid shared with the music bed, so it renders with no footage, models or downloads.

option_3.description: The third possible answer, copied from the brief; fill it whenever the quiz has three or more answers (der, die, das). Leave it out only for a two-answer quiz

option_4.description: The fourth possible answer, copied from the brief; leave it out unless the quiz has four answers

copy_examples.brief: Quiz reel for Cellar Door, a Spanish class in Leeds. Is it el or la? Five words with their meanings: agua (water) is el, mano (hand) is la, problema (problem) is el, foto (photo) is la, día (day) is el. One-line reasons to show: agua is 'el agua: dodges la agua' (it stays feminine); mano is 'feminine, despite the -o'; problema is 'Greek -ma words: masculine'; foto is 'short for fotografía'; día is 'masculine, despite the -a'. End with 'Book a free trial class' and cellardoorspanish.co.uk.
copy_examples.note: Two options, so option_3 and option_4 are left out. Every word, answer, meaning and reason is copied from the brief; the writer only composed the hook, kicker and outro. Articles read best with the prefix style ('el agua').

copy_examples.brief: Trivia short for the Orbit Club astronomy society: planet or moon? Titan is a moon (of Saturn), Mercury is a planet (smallest one), Ganymede is a moon (bigger than Mercury), Venus is a planet (hottest planet), Europa is a moon (ice-covered ocean). Call to action: Join us at the next stargazing night.

inputs.cta: Join us at the next stargazing night

copy_examples.note: The brief's answers are lower case ('a moon'); options are copied in title case and answers match them. No link was given, so none is shown; reasons are the brief's own words.

style.typography: Inter ExtraBold/Black, centred cards, bins labelled in their option colour

direction.action: Hook, five timed rounds (drop in, 3-2-1, reveal with reason, drop into the bin), recap and call to action

notes: The animation is code (recipes/scene/quiz-challenge) rendered frame-exactly on a virtual clock; the writer supplies the copy and three choices only.

Questions, answers, hints, reasons, options, the call to action and the link are verbatim: they must come from the brief, because a quiz that teaches a wrong answer is worse than no video. Each answer must equal one of the options; the scene throws (and check_inputs reports it) otherwise.
Hints and reasons are all-or-none: give one for every question or leave them all out.

Beat grid 112.5 bpm (16 frames a beat): hook frames 0-48; round k (0-4) starts at frame 48 + 96k with ticks at +12, +24, +36, the reveal and chime at +48, and the drop whoosh at +76; outro from frame 528 with the call to action at 561. The music bed runs at the same tempo, so every reveal lands on a beat.
The poster frame (36) shows the coloured hook over the bins: a cover that states the challenge.
The contact sheet shows round 1's countdown (78), each reveal with its reason on screen (110, 206, 302, 398, 494) and the outro recap (600).
output.silent_cut also delivers <name>.silent.mp4 (picture only) for posting with in-app trending sound; the mastered cut with ticks, chimes and the bed stays the main deliverable.

quality_gates.description: Integrated loudness lands within 1 LU of the -14 LUFS delivery target.
Decoded true peak stays at or below -0.5 dBTP after AAC encoding.
No stretch of blank picture (no visible contrast, any colour) lasts longer than 0.5 seconds.
A subject expert checks every answer, hint and reason against a trusted source; one wrong answer misteaches every viewer.
A reviewer confirms the hook, call to action and link are accurate and approved for publication.
